newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Aspiration senses win in Thai vote.
newsitem.headline: New Aspiration senses win in Thai vote.

text.p: The leader of the New Aspiration Party (NAP), Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, said on Sunday he sensed victory in the Thai election.

Appearing with the leaders of four other parties, expected to align with the NAP if it won the polls, he said: "We are here together to show that we are victorious...but we should be patient, taking one step at a time."
Television and radio stations are divided over whether the NAP or the Democrats would win the election. Official results are not expected until Monday morning.
But one of the party leaders who appeared with Chavalit at the news conference said he projected the five parties would jointly control a total of over 200 seats in the 393-seat parliament.
Chavalit said the leaders had gathered to show that they were prepared to work together in future even though no definite pact had been reached to form a coalition.

Earlier, Democrat leader and former premier Chuan Leekpai said he acknowledged that the NAP might be leading marginally according to unofficial television projections. But after he spoke, the projections changed to show a tie betwen the NAP and the Democrats.
